newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet set to return to U.S. skies Monday.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet set to return to U.S. skies Monday.

text.p: U.S. discount carrier ValuJet Inc, a former darling on Wall Street but the bane of other airlines, was scheduled to return to the skies Monday for the first time since its grounding three months ago.

With an opening barrage of advertising, the airline launched an aggressive bid over the weekend to lure passengers back to its no-frills service by offering one-way fares of just $19 for flights between Atlanta and four other U.S. cities, including Washington, D.C.

Rival airlines are already braced for the return of ultra-low fares. On Friday, Atlanta-based Delta Air Lines Inc. said it would match the $19 introductory ValuJet fares, which run through Thursday. Kiwi International Air Lines said it also would adopt a similar strategy.

"We've done our homework. We have prepared for Game Day. Game Day is here. We're ready for the whistle to blow and we'll be out there doing a great job," ValuJet President Lewis Jordan told reporters after announcing the carrier's return.

ValuJet came under intense scrutiny from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) after the May 11 crash of Flight 592 in the Florida Evergrades, which killed all 110 passengers and crew members on board.

A cause has not yet been determined, but investigators think oxygen generators that were improperly stored in the plane's cargo hold by a subcontractor may have ignited, causing a fire that led to the crash.

But in the aftermath of the disaster, FAA inspectors also found widespread maintenance problems at ValuJet, and in mid-June forced the airline to ground its fleet of 51 planes. An intensive 15-week project to overhaul the airline's operations ensued.
The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) finally declared ValuJet fit to fly again last Thursday. By midday on Friday, the airline had rung up about 7,000 bookings.
With a skeleton staff and a fleet of only five DC-9s, the newly resurrected ValuJet was set to begin scheduled service at 12:30 p.m. (1630 GMT) on Monday with a flight to Washington's Dulles airport.

Initially, the carrier also will fly to Orlando, Tampa and Fort Lauderdale, Florida. Plans call for the addition of another 12 destinations by Oct. 24, by which time its one-way fares will have risen to $49.
But a union for airline flight attendants was still trying to halt ValuJet's rebirth in federal court.

On Friday, the Association of Flight Attendants asked the U.S. Court of Appeals in Washington to block the airline's return pending a union appeal to have Jordan and ValuJet Chairman Robert Priddy ousted from management.
The union, which accuses the two men of putting profits ahead of safety during the months preceding the Everglades crash, has launched an appeal of the DOT's approval.
